title: A Quantum Roadmap for Softmax Attention: Exact Born-Rule Analogs for Softmax Attention on the Probability Simplex
authors: Eric A. F. Reinhardt, Adam J. Hauser
abstract: The attention mechanism forms the foundation of many modern AI models such as the Transformer. In one subclass of problems where attention is used, inputs and outputs are bound to the probability simplex so that all outputs sum to one. In this setting, softmax attention admits an exact, component-by-component quantum realization. Attention scores are Hadamard-test statistics on block-encoded projections of amplitude-encoded inputs. The exponential softmax is the interior of a cosine-squared family generated by Born-rule measurement under an exact bijection, whose boundary expresses sparse attention with exact zeros at finite parameter values. The softmax temperature is a repetition count where post-selected measurement rounds realize discretized inverse temperature exactly. Value aggregation is a deterministic column-loading channel that dilates the column-stochastic value matrix. The gated residual is the preparation angle of a single ancilla, with the additive identity at a mixing angle of π/2. Every learnable parameter is a rotation-gate angle. The composed layer is exact in the infinite-shot limit with one measure-and-reload step per attention score; a fully-coherent variant is ε-approximate via quantum singular value transformation in the infinite depth limit. The algebraic core is machine-checked in Lean 4.
summary: This paper constructs a detailed quantum circuit realization for the attention mechanism used in Transformers, specifically when inputs are probability distributions. It shows that core components like softmax and temperature can be mapped exactly to sequences of quantum measurements and rotations. This work bridges advanced deep learning architectures with fundamental principles of quantum information processing.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop an exact, component-by-component quantum realization for the softmax attention mechanism, particularly when inputs are constrained to the probability simplex.
main_result: It establishes that softmax attention admits such a quantum analog in the infinite-shot limit, mapping classical components like temperature and residual connections to specific quantum gates and measurement protocols.
method: The realization uses quantum primitives including amplitude encoding, block-encoded projections, Hadamard tests for inner products, and controlled rotations ($	ext{c}R_y$) within a circuit framework.
model_or_system: The model is the single-head gated transformer attention layer operating on inputs restricted to the probability simplex. The computation is mapped onto a quantum circuit utilizing qubits and unitary transformations.
key_observables: Attention scores, which are realized as Hadamard-test statistics on block-encoded projections of amplitude-encoded inputs.
important_parameters: The softmax temperature ($ eta$) is physically realized by the number ($L$) of post-selected measurement rounds; learnable parameters correspond to rotation-gate angles.
main_assumptions: The equivalence is exact only in the infinite-shot limit. The construction assumes inputs are row-normalized probability distributions (the probability simplex domain).
figures_summary: Figure 1 provides a 'dictionary at a glance' mapping classical components to quantum circuits; Figure 2 illustrates Born-rule encoding, and Figure 3 shows Q/K projection using block encoding.
paper_structure: The paper builds an equivalence dictionary by realizing core attention components (scores, softmax, temperature, residual) sequentially. It details the necessary quantum primitives for each classical function, culminating in a full layer equivalence theorem machine-checked in Lean 4.
why_interesting: While focused on AI, the rigorous mapping of continuous mathematical functions (like softmax) to discrete quantum operations (Born measurements, rotations) provides deep insights into how complex classical computations can be fundamentally constrained or realized within quantum information theory.
